data.note:
Error reflection: true MoA Eg5 inhibitors, I called Microtubule stabilizers.

Both classes arrest in mitosis with rounded bright-DNA cells and dense tubulin, so tub_mean z=+28.5 / contrast z=+40.2 misled me. Eg5 inhibition produces monopolar spindles with a dense tubulin rosette (classic monastrol phenotype PMID:10542155; K858 Eg5 inhibitor PMID:19351824; monopolar spindle formation PMID:31679979), which at this resolution mimics stabilizer bundling/hyper-polymerization (taxol-like epothilone action PMID:7757983).

Key mistake: atlas mean similarity actually favored Eg5 (0.855) over stabilizers (0.828) despite 6/10 count for stabilizers, and microscopist flagged inability to resolve monopolarity vs multipolarity. I over-weighted bulk tubulin intensity and majority vote.

Next time: require spindle-polarity readout (pericentrin/gamma-tubulin foci count per pH3+ cell + high-res tubulin) to split Eg5 monopolar rosettes from stabilizer bundled/multipolar spindles, plus in vitro tubulin polymerization control.

reflection.text:
We saw concordant, dose-scaled tubulin elevation at 1 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z +40.2, tub_mean z +28.5) and 0.03 uM (tub_std z +19.4) with high DNA content (nuc_dna_integrated z +19.8), low nuclear solidity and lower density, plus a visual report of bright tubulin with rounded mitotic cells and 6/10 atlas neighbours as microtubule stabilizers, so we concluded stabilizers at p=0.78 with Eg5 second at 0.22.

That tubulin-intensity logic was the error: a monopolar Eg5 spindle also converges microtubules into a bright dense rosette that can inflate tub_mean, tub_std and contrast in low-resolution features, as in the classic spindle-bipolarity inhibitor phenotype (PMID 10542155) and monopolar-spindle induction by Eg5 inhibition (PMID 31679979), while condensed DNA and low solidity only report shared mitotic arrest. We over-weighted the 6/10 vs 4/10 neighbour count and the e4 stabilizer label and under-weighted that mean atlas similarity slightly favored Eg5 and that 4/10 Eg5 neighbours made Eg5 a strong runner-up, and we treated bright tubulin as stabilizer-specific bundling like epothilones/taxol (PMID 7757983) without evidence.

The acquisition choices left no way to recover: we spent the 2-well budget on two different doses with no same-dose replicate and no spindle-polarity readout, so we could show dose-consistency but not replicate reliability or monopolar vs bundled morphology. Tubulin amount/texture alone cannot separate stabilization from monopolar convergence.
what_was_right: Recognized dose-consistent mitotic arrest from two doses: lower density, high nuc_dna_integrated, very low nuc_solidity and rounded mitotic cells.
Correctly rejected microtubule destabilizers because tubulin intensity/texture massively increased rather than decreased.
Kept Eg5 inhibitors as an explicit runner-up because atlas showed 4/10 Eg5 neighbours and mitotic arrest overlapped.
what_was_wrong: Misinterpreted tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2, tub_mean z=+28.5 and tub_std z=+19.4 as stabilizer-specific bundling, when Eg5 monopolar rosettes also concentrate tubulin signal.
Over-weighted atlas vote count (6/10 stabilizers vs 4/10 Eg5) and e4 visual label while discounting higher mean similarity for Eg5 and shared mitotic features.
Used both wells on different doses (1 uM and 0.03 uM rep 1) with no same-dose replicate and no centrosome/spindle-polarity imaging, so monopolar vs bundled spindles were never tested.

# MuseCell dossier · specimen s_7526ba207c

Run `run_29df2c4384ea` · blinded · 2026-10-29 10:08 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3-contributor, microscopist muse-spark-1.3-contributor, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image)

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (2 of 2 wells)

| Evidence | Dose (µM) | Replicate | Cells | Strongest changes vs DMSO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e2 | 1 | 1 | 295 | tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2; tub_mean z=+28.5; nuc_solidity z=-28.3 |
| e3 | 0.03 | 1 | 295 | nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.8; tub_std z=+19.4; nuc_solidity z=-19.1 |

## Steps

1. `list_available_experiments` — Need dose list and budget to plan discriminative wells.
2. `acquire_well` — Highest dose should show strongest phenotype for MoA discrimination.
3. `acquire_well` — Mid dose to test dose-dependence and separate specific vs toxic effects.
4. `describe_phenotype` — Visual check of high-dose microtubule bundles vs mitotic arrest to separate stabilizers.
5. `compare_to_reference_atlas` — Nearest reference MoAs will discriminate stabilizers from other mitotics.
6. `update_hypotheses` — Large tub increase at both doses plus mitotics favors stabilizers; atlas Eg5 overlap keeps Eg5 second.
7. `submit_conclusion` — Massive tubulin increase at two doses with mitotic condensed DNA and atlas taxol/epothilone neighbours favors stabilizers over Eg5.
8. `lookup_compound` — Protocol step after the review: identify the unblinded specimen in PubChem and ChEMBL.
9. `search_literature` — Need real papers on Eg5 inhibition phenotype to explain mitotic arrest overlap.
10. `search_literature` — Need stabilizer phenotype papers to contrast why tubulin increase misled us.
11. `lookup_compound` — Atlas top Eg5 neighbour; check its curated mechanism to understand similarity. *(error: Neither PubChem nor ChEMBL knows 'AZ138'.)*

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: Microtubule stabilizers 0.68, Eg5 inhibitors 0.22, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.05, Microtubule destabilizers 0.05

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.78); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e5.

Why: Massive tubulin increase at two doses with mitotic condensed DNA and atlas taxol/epothilone neighbours favors stabilizers over Eg5.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: High-resolution anti-alpha-tubulin + pericentrin + pH3 immunofluorescence to score spindle polarity/bundling: stabilizers show bundled microtubules/multipolar spindles vs Eg5 monopolar rosettes; plus in vitro tubulin polymerization assay.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

**Approve — Microtubule stabilizers justified.** Two doses (1 µM dose‑7 and 0.03 µM dose‑4, rep‑1) show concordant, massive, dose‑scaled tubulin elevation (tub_mean z +28.5→+17.0, tub_glcm_contrast +40.2→+13.4) with condensed DNA, so this is not a weak/single‑well artifact, though a same‑dose replicate is absent. Phenotype (e4: bright bundled tubulin, rounded mitotic cells) and atlas (6/10 neighbours stabilizers from two reference compounds vs 4/10 Eg5 from one compound) favour stabilizers. Eg5 explains mitotic arrest but not the marked tubulin intensity/texture rise, particularly at 0.03 µM where frac_mitotic_like z = –0.38; destabilizers are contradicted. Atlas mean similarity being slightly higher for Eg5 (0.855 vs 0.828) keeps Eg5 a real runner‑up, making 0.78 at the high end but defensible; budget is exhausted and further low‑resolution imaging would not resolve spindle polarity.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ-C** (no PubChem record shown)

Identity check: BBBC021 gives no structure for this compound (an internal code); name matches in PubChem would be unrelated compounds, so none is shown

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Eg5 inhibitors**.

## Reflection

We saw concordant, dose-scaled tubulin elevation at 1 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z +40.2, tub_mean z +28.5) and 0.03 uM (tub_std z +19.4) with high DNA content (nuc_dna_integrated z +19.8), low nuclear solidity and lower density, plus a visual report of bright tubulin with rounded mitotic cells and 6/10 atlas neighbours as microtubule stabilizers, so we concluded stabilizers at p=0.78 with Eg5 second at 0.22.

That tubulin-intensity logic was the error: a monopolar Eg5 spindle also converges microtubules into a bright dense rosette that can inflate tub_mean, tub_std and contrast in low-resolution features, as in the classic spindle-bipolarity inhibitor phenotype (PMID 10542155) and monopolar-spindle induction by Eg5 inhibition (PMID 31679979), while condensed DNA and low solidity only report shared mitotic arrest. We over-weighted the 6/10 vs 4/10 neighbour count and the e4 stabilizer label and under-weighted that mean atlas similarity slightly favored Eg5 and that 4/10 Eg5 neighbours made Eg5 a strong runner-up, and we treated bright tubulin as stabilizer-specific bundling like epothilones/taxol (PMID 7757983) without evidence.

The acquisition choices left no way to recover: we spent the 2-well budget on two different doses with no same-dose replicate and no spindle-polarity readout, so we could show dose-consistency but not replicate reliability or monopolar vs bundled morphology. Tubulin amount/texture alone cannot separate stabilization from monopolar convergence.

What was right:
- Recognized dose-consistent mitotic arrest from two doses: lower density, high nuc_dna_integrated, very low nuc_solidity and rounded mitotic cells.
- Correctly rejected microtubule destabilizers because tubulin intensity/texture massively increased rather than decreased.
- Kept Eg5 inhibitors as an explicit runner-up because atlas showed 4/10 Eg5 neighbours and mitotic arrest overlapped.

What was wrong or missed:
- Misinterpreted tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2, tub_mean z=+28.5 and tub_std z=+19.4 as stabilizer-specific bundling, when Eg5 monopolar rosettes also concentrate tubulin signal.
- Over-weighted atlas vote count (6/10 stabilizers vs 4/10 Eg5) and e4 visual label while discounting higher mean similarity for Eg5 and shared mitotic features.
- Used both wells on different doses (1 uM and 0.03 uM rep 1) with no same-dose replicate and no centrosome/spindle-polarity imaging, so monopolar vs bundled spindles were never tested.

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution alpha-tubulin plus pericentrin/centrosome and DNA immunofluorescence to score spindle polarity in mitotics (Eg5 monopolar rosettes vs stabilizer bundles/multipolar spindles), paired with a cell-free tubulin polymerization assay which should be negative for a pure Eg5 inhibitor.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [10542155](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10542155/): Small molecule inhibitor of mitotic spindle bipolarity identified in a phenotype-based screen. *Science* (1999) — Small-molecule inhibition of Eg5 blocks mitotic spindle bipolarity, producing monopolar spindles and mitotic arrest.
- PMID [31679979](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31679979/): Pyrenocine A induces monopolar spindle formation and suppresses proliferation of cancer cells. *Bioorg Med Chem* (2019) — Eg5 inhibition induces monopolar spindle formation with proliferation suppression.
- PMID [7757983](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7757983/): Epothilones, a new class of microtubule-stabilizing agents with a taxol-like mechanism of action. *Cancer Res* (1995) — Epothilones act as microtubule-stabilizing agents with a taxol-like mechanism.
